sourceObligations.sourceAnchor: The stem of any kind of agentive NNC names the agent of an action (compare the English agentives "preacher," i.e., one who preach…
The most common kind of agentive NNC is the preterit-agentive NNC.
Like all nounstems, a preterit-agentive nounstem has two shapes-restricted use and general use.
The general- use stem is a compound that uses the restricted-use stem as its embed.
The restricted-use stem is simply the predicate of a preterit-tense VNC.
The restricted-use stem is used in absolutive-state NNCs.
The restricted-use stem is discussed first.
The general-use stem is used everywhere else.
